children: Australian stocks look set to extend their recovery from their recent three-month low despite a mixed lead from U.S. equities. ASX futures are up 0.2% ahead of Wednesday's open, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 benchmark index will add to the 0.3% rise eked out across the prior session. Ahead of the open, IAG said it would reapply for permission to buy a Western Australia state insurer after the country's competition regulator opposed the transaction for a second time. In the U.S., the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to a record, and the S&P 500 was nearly unchanged. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
